answers.answer: Shuffle the nine region cards; reveal the top and place the King in that region. Each player takes another card to set their home region and puts their Grande there. Of ten initial Caballeros, put two in the home region, one on the first success-track space, and seven in the court.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'reveal the top card and put the King in that region'; 'another region card to determine their home region'; ten are split two, one, and seven.

answers.answer: In round 1, players choose who begins. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round begins; others play clockwise. A power-card value already played that round cannot be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'Players choose who begins playing power cards in round 1'; later the preceding round's last-turn player begins; others play 'clockwise'; 'No value already played this round may be matched.'

answers.answer: Turns go in descending power-card value. At the start of your turn, recruit up to the Caballero allowance pictured on your power card from provinces into your court (you may recruit fewer); then choose an action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'Take turns in descending power-card value'; 'At the start of your turn recruit up to'; after recruitment, choose an available face-up action card.

answers.answer: If your provinces lack enough of your color, you may take your own Caballeros from the board to make up the difference. The King's region cannot supply them, and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'you may take your own from the board to make up the difference. The King's region remains taboo and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.'

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment moves from your court to regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or the Castillo, dividing the allowance freely. The printed number is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none. The deployment may be divided among destinations, but it is one activity and cannot be split around the special action.
answers.evidence: Ordinary deployment: 'maximum'; deploy from court to 'any regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or the Castillo, dividing the allowance freely'; may deploy fewer, including none. Activities cannot be split or interleaved.

answers.answer: Yes. Do ordinary deployment and the special action in either order, but complete one activity before beginning the other; neither may be interleaved or split. The special action may be declined.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'Do them in either order, but complete one activity before starting the other'; 'You may decline the special action.'

answers.answer: After a player's turn, lay their selected action card aside so later players cannot choose it. After all players have acted, discard any remaining face-up action cards. The King card is revealed again every round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'Lay aside the selected action card'; discard remaining face-up cards after every player has taken a turn; King card 'never permanently discarded.'

answers.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King's region. It may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected; King-moving actions are the exception to the taboo. Ordinary deployment uses the King's new location if the King is moved first, and the old location if deployment is first.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: 'no Caballero, Grande or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of it'; 'It may still be scored'; moving the King changes which region is protected.

answers.answer: Clearly announce how many Caballeros you put in the Castillo. Entry is allowed regardless of the King's location. Pieces cannot leave by an action; they leave only during general scoring.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: Caballeros may go into Castillo 'regardless of the King's location'; 'Announce clearly how many'; 'leave only during general scoring.'

answers.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. In order: (1) before uncovering the Castillo, each player secretly sets a disk to any board region except the King's region and places it face down; (2) uncover and score the Castillo; (3) reveal disks and move each player's Castillo pieces to that one selected region, except pieces whose destination is the King's region go to their owner's court, then replace the Castillo empty; (4) score the nine regions in scoring-track order and record points.
answers.evidence: General scoring: 'after rounds 3, 6 and 9'; stages specify secretly select destinations before uncovering, score Castillo, reveal/empty, then score nine regions.

answers.answer: Each player sends all their Castillo Caballeros to one region; they cannot split them or keep any in the Castillo. The disk choice excludes the King's region, but if a player selected it, those pieces go to that player's court instead.
answers.evidence: General scoring: 'All that player's Castillo Caballeros must go to one region'; disks select any board region except King's; Castillo is replaced empty. If someone selected King's region, pieces go to court.

answers.answer: The three players tied for first each receive the second-place value, 3 points; the player with three Caballeros receives the third-place value, 1 point. Grandes do not count toward majority; only Caballeros count.
answers.evidence: Region ranks examples: on 5/3/1 counts 4,4,4,3 score 3,3,3,1. 'Only Caballeros count toward majority. A Grande ... contributes zero Caballeros.'

answers.answer: The player with 4 scores 6; the player with 3 scores 4; both players tied at 2 score 0 each.
answers.evidence: Region ranks examples: on 6/4/2, counts 4,3,2,2 score 6,4,0,0.

answers.answer: In a two-player game, only first place can pay; in a three-player game, first and second can pay. A two-player tie for first shifts to second place, which is outside the two-player payable ranks, so neither scores.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: 'Two players: only first place can pay. Three players: only first and second can pay'; 'a two-player tie for first pays neither player.'

answers.answer: Whenever the relevant region is scored, including during special scoring, the sole majority holder in the King's region gets +2, and the sole majority holder with their own Grande in a region gets +2. Neither bonus applies on a tie for first.
answers.evidence: Bonuses apply whenever the relevant region is scored, 'including special scorings'; King's bonus +2 for sole majority in King's region; Home bonus +2 for sole majority with own Grande; neither on tie.

answers.answer: No. Special scoring uncovers and scores the Castillo, then covers the same Caballeros again; they are not redistributed and wait there until general scoring.
answers.evidence: Protected locations and Stack 3: special scoring 'reveals and scores its contents, then covers them again without redistribution'; Castillo card covers the same Caballeros.

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be placed in the Castillo. It may not move into or out of the King's region. The two scoreboards cannot be stacked, and they cannot be reversed or rotated to create other values; use them right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Mobile scoreboard: 'Castillo is allowed'; no movement into/out of King's region; cannot stack; place right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0.

answers.answer: Move your Grande to another region, but not into the King's region or Castillo; it cannot leave the King's region. Other Grandes may already be in the destination. The destination becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Grande: 'another region except the King's region or Castillo'; 'It cannot leave the King's region'; destination may contain several Grandes; becomes new home region.

answers.answer: Return any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the one played this turn. You need not reveal which card you take, although taking the visible top card is apparent.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Power Cards: 'any one of your played power cards ... including the one played this turn'; 'You need not reveal which.'

answers.answer: The standard game ends after the third general scoring, after round 9 and after all its stages (including scoring the final regions). The player furthest along the success track wins; there is no additional tiebreaker stated.
answers.evidence: Overview and End: game ends 'after the third general scoring'; finish all stages after round 9; furthest along success track wins; no additional tiebreaker.

answers.answer: Separate the action cards into five stacks according to the 1–5 Caballeros printed on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place them face down by the board. Reveal the top card of each of the five stacks at the start of each round. The standard round marker starts at 1.
answers.evidence: Setup: separate and shuffle each stack; standard round marker at 1. Turn Structure: reveal the top card of each of five action stacks each round.

answers.answer: No. Played power cards remain in each player's face-up used stack; only its top card is visible, rather than returning to hand. A special action can recover a played card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: played cards 'remain in each player's face-up used stack with only the top card visible, rather than returning to hand'; a special action can recover one.

answers.answer: If the King card's special action moves the King before deployment, the new position controls which regions are adjacent for deployment. The King may be placed in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: King card: put King in 'any region except Castillo'; use King's current location at time of deployment. Protected locations explains new position if King moved before deployment.

answers.answer: Keep the Veto card before you for use during this round or the next. It can stop one special action, but cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion of an action card.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Veto: 'Put the card before you and retain it to stop one special action during this round or the next'; 'It cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion.'

answers.answer: While a Veto is held, other players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as the player starts: it can stop an announced action before execution or prevent the remaining part of an incomplete action. It cannot undo completed parts; a partial veto leaves already executed parts in effect.
answers.evidence: Veto: players must announce special actions; object as soon as the player starts; may stop before execution or prevent remaining part; completed actions cannot be vetoed and executed parts are not undone.

answers.answer: Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
answers.evidence: Veto: 'Discard after using the veto once; if unused, discard at the end of the next round.'

answers.answer: Every fellow player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces; a player with an empty court sends none. The selecting player is unaffected.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority — all court: every fellow player sends all court Caballeros to provinces; empty court sends none; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The fellow player with two sends both to the provinces because they have fewer than three. If you are the selecting player with five, you are unaffected and keep all five.
answers.evidence: Three-from-court Decay: every fellow player sends three, 'or all they have if fewer than three'; selecting player is unaffected.

answers.answer: The detailed execution says each player, including the selecting player, returns three of their own Caballeros to the provinces. Begin with the player to the selecting player's left, proceed clockwise, and have the selecting player go last. Each chooses their own pieces from any regions and/or their court, never from the King's region or Castillo. The bold heading says 'fellow players,' unlike the detailed paragraph and matching card face, which say each player. The summary reports no explicit shortfall rule if a player has fewer than three eligible pieces.
answers.evidence: The King returns: detailed paragraph/card say each player including selecting player sends three; order begins left and proceeds clockwise, selector last; sources any regions/court except King's region/Castillo; heading says 'fellow players'; no explicit shortfall rule.

answers.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each chosen piece to its owner's provinces. No pieces may be taken from courts, the King's region, or the Castillo. The summary gives no fallback if a player has no eligible piece.
answers.evidence: Send one from each player: selecting player chooses one from a region for each player including themselves; no taking from courts, King's region or Castillo; no explicit fallback for no eligible piece.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses one region on their disk; choices are simultaneous and revealed together. The region must contain at least two of that player's Caballeros, and they return two to the provinces. The source does not explain disk selection if the only pieces are in the protected King's region.
answers.evidence: Fellow players secretly remove two: each affected fellow player secretly chooses a region; choices simultaneous/revealed together; it must contain at least two of that player's Caballeros; return two.

answers.answer: If the fellow player has no legal region with two but has single Caballeros in legal regions, they choose a region containing one and return that one to the provinces.
answers.evidence: Secretly remove two: 'If the player has at most one in every region, choose a region with one and return that one.'

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses on a disk a region containing at least one of their Caballeros; choices are revealed together. They return all their own Caballeros in that chosen region to the provinces. A player with none in any region is unaffected.
answers.evidence: Secretly remove all from one region: simultaneous secret disk selection; choose a region with at least one own Caballero and return all there; player with none in any region unaffected.

answers.answer: Yes, the player may choose any region, including the King's region, or the Castillo. Normal region-scoring rules, applicable rank limits, and bonuses apply. If Castillo is chosen, it is scored and covered with the same pieces again; they are not redistributed.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Pick one region to score: any region including King's region or Castillo; normal rules/rank limits/bonuses; if Castillo, cover the same pieces again without distribution.

answers.answer: The printed 4-value group is Galicia (4/2/0), Catalonia (4/2/1), and Seville (4/3/1). Eligibility is determined by a region's current first value, including any mobile scoreboard replacing its printed values. Thus Galicia with 8/4/0 does not qualify, while Granada with 4/0/0 does. Applicable bonuses apply to these special scorings.
answers.evidence: Stack 3: regions whose current first value is 4; printed group listed; mobile 8/4/0 in Galicia removes it and 4/0/0 in Granada adds Granada. Special scorings apply home and King's bonuses.

answers.answer: The printed 5-value group is Basque Country, Aragon, and Valencia; the printed 6-and-7 group is Old Castile, New Castile, and Granada. A mobile scoreboard replaces printed values for both points and category eligibility, so membership follows the current first value. Castillo is not scored by all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 lists the printed groups and says mobile scoreboard replaces printed values for both points and category eligibility; all-5 explicitly says Castillo is not scored.

answers.answer: Only sole first places score; a tie for first receives the normal second-place value and therefore scores nothing under this card. All lower ranks score nothing. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 first-position-only: only sole first places score; tie for first scores nothing since it normally pays second; other ranks get nothing; excludes Castillo.

answers.answer: Both board regions tied for the most total Caballeros are scored. The Castillo is neither considered nor scored, even if it contains more pieces than either region.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 most-Caballeros card: score all regions tied for the most; Castillo is neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: Compare nonempty board regions; empty regions are excluded. Score all regions tied for the least among those nonempty regions. The Castillo is neither considered nor scored.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 least-Caballeros card: compare nonempty board regions, score all tied for least; empty regions and Castillo neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: All fellow players move all their own Caballeros out of the chosen region. Each affected player secretly chooses another region with their disk, and choices are revealed simultaneously. A player choosing the King's region or the region being vacated sends their group to their own court instead. The King's-region taboo prevents taking pieces out of that region, and Castillo cannot be emptied with this card.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Movement: all fellow players move all their own Caballeros out; each secretly chooses another region, reveal simultaneously; choosing King's region or vacated region sends pieces to court; taboo and Castillo restriction follow.

answers.answer: Royal Adviser moves the King at most one region, to a neighboring region. The King card may place him in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Royal Adviser: 'neighboring region', no more than one region away. King card: any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: The Court moves two of your own Caballeros from the provinces to your court. This is separate from a 4-stack card's normal deployment of up to four from court to board; the two activities can be done in either order, completing one before the other. The summary gives no explicit shortfall procedure if provinces cannot supply both.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 The Court: two own Caballeros from provinces to court; separate from normal up-to-four court-to-board deployment; either activity can go first; no explicit shortfall procedure.

answers.answer: All players secretly choose regions on disks and reveal simultaneously. A uniquely chosen region is scored under normal rules; if multiple players chose the same region, it is not scored. The disk permits nine board regions including the King's region, but not the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: all players choose secretly and reveal simultaneously; score each uniquely chosen region; duplicate choice is not scored; disk allows nine board regions including King's region but not Castillo.

answers.answer: You may take all your own Caballeros from one origin region and distribute them among other regions and/or the Castillo; you may return some to the original region. Origins exclude the King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King's region but may include Castillo. Ordinary deployment still has its separate adjacency restriction.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 Intrigue: all own from one region; distribute among other regions and/or Castillo; may return some to original. Origins exclude King's region/Castillo; destinations exclude King's but may include Castillo.

answers.answer: The special action adds up to two more own Caballeros from court; with normal deployment of up to one, as many as three may enter the board. Only the normal one requires adjacency to the King's region; the two special-action pieces may go to any non-King region and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: 'Two more from court' up to two additional to any non-King regions and/or Castillo; with normal one, up to three enter, but only normal one requires adjacency.

answers.answer: No. Choose one special alternative: add up to two more from court or move all your own Caballeros from one region. The normal deployment of up to one still applies.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: choose one of the preceding special actions, not both; normal deployment still applies.

answers.answer: The action moves up to five own and/or foreign Caballeros, but all must come from one origin region. They may be distributed to other non-King regions and/or the Castillo; they cannot return to the origin region under this action.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: 'Up to five own and/or foreign Caballeros from one origin region,' distributed to 'other non-King regions and/or Castillo.'

answers.answer: You may move up to three foreign Caballeros only; your own pieces cannot be included. They may come from any regions, including multiple origins. Destinations are any non-King regions and/or the Castillo. The number is a maximum, so fewer are permitted.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: 'Any three foreign' means up to three other players' Caballeros from any regions, including multiple origins; destinations exclude King's region but may include Castillo.

answers.answer: The any-three action allows up to three own and/or foreign Caballeros from any non-King origin regions to any non-King regions and/or the Castillo. The any-four action allows up to four own and/or foreign pieces from any non-King origins, but destinations must be other non-King regions and/or Castillo. These actions allow mixed ownership and flexible origins; the four-piece card's destination rule is stricter because it says 'other regions.'
answers.evidence: Stack 1: any three own/foreign from any non-King origin regions to any non-King destinations; any four own/foreign from non-King origins into other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: Move up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros; these are separate ownership allowances. Pieces may come from any regions (multiple origins are allowed). Origins exclude the King's region and Castillo under the general Intrigue restrictions; destinations exclude the King's region and may include Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: 'Up to two of your own plus two foreign' are separate ownership allowances, from any regions. General table rules: origins exclude King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude King's but may include Castillo.

answers.answer: Move up to four Caballeros, own pieces only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or the Castillo. Castillo cannot be an origin; the destination must be different from each origin region.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: any four own only from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo; general Intrigue origin rules exclude Castillo.

answers.answer: For the 4-stack secret-choice scoring action, players may select any of the nine board regions, including the King's region, but may not select Castillo; duplicate selections are not scored and unique selections are. This differs from the pick-one-location action, where its player may choose any region including the King's region or Castillo, and Castillo is scored but covered again without redistribution.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 secret scoring: disk permits nine board regions including King's region but not Castillo; unique regions score and duplicates do not. Stack 2 pick one region: includes King's region or Castillo; Castillo pieces remain and are covered again.
